3. The applicants herein are the husband, brother-in-law, mother-in-law, and sister-in-law of non-applicant No.2.

The applicants herein seeks quashment of Regular Criminal Case No. 182/2024 arising out of chargesheet dated 03/05/2024 in Crime No. 0267 of 2019, registered for the offence punishable under Sections 307, 313, 498A, 504 and 506 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
4.

The story of prosecution in the present case in short is that, the non-applicant No. 2 lodged a police complaint against the present applicants alleging that they were demanding rkn 3 apl 345.2020 new (1).odt Rs.5,00,000/- for starting a hospital by Applicant/husband.
It is alleged that thereafter a hospital was constructed at village Reulgaon and mother-in-law used to visit them at the said village.

It is further alleged that husband of non-applicant No.2 used to quarrel with her on the ground that instead of opening the hospital in a village, the same should have been started at District Place, and therefore again harassed non-applicant No.2 on that count.
5. It is alleged that during the period of pregnancy, she was not given proper treatment by Applicants.
There were twice compromise between her and Applicants in the meeting of Elders of both family, but Applicants keep continue their harassment against her.
She alleged that on 23/03/2018, Applicants forcibly consumed her poison.
Therefore, they took her hospital and then shifted to Government Hospital on next day.
After that she went with her parents at Vasmat.
After that she received legal notice of divorce from Applicant Husband.
Then she went to Womans Cell at Hingoli, but Applicant Husband did not attend the counselling proceeding.

Therefore, she lodged police complaint against Applicants on her complaint offence is registered against Applicants under Sections 307, 498A, 313, 504 and 506 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code.

Accordingly, it was again decided that the parties should cohabit and enjoy their martial life.

Thereafter, non-applicant No.2 in the month of September 2019 filed the complaint against the applicants and his family members under the provisions of Protection of Woman from Domestic Violence Act.

On that day, there was a food poison to the non-applicant No.2 and therefore, applicant No.1 has informed this fact to his neighbour and with the help of neighbourer namely Amol Ramesh Podhade, he has immediately taken the non-applicant No.2 at Hospital.
In the hospital, necessary treatment was given to her and accordingly she was became normal within a day.
No such case is registered either at Hospital where she as admitted nor in the Government Hospital where she alleged to be admitted after such incidences.

In the light of the submissions made by the learned Counsel for both sides before this Court, it would be relevant to consider Section 498-A of IPC.

The bare perusal of this provision shows that vide its Explanation -(a) the cruelty means any wilfil conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive a woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical) of a woman.

As per Explanation - (b) harassment is done with a view to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to meet such demand.
As such, while deciding these allegations, this Court has to first look into whether the cruelty which is allegedly falls in the explanation provided under Section 498-A of IPC or not.

12. It is also pertinent to note that the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India and this Court has experienced that there is a tendency of implicating the husband and his relatives in the criminal offence on vague and omnibous allegations.
Therefore, this Court is required to be extremely careful and cautions in dealing with these complaints and must take pragmatic realities into consideration while dealing with matrimonial cases.
13 To attract the offence, it is necessary that the allegations levelled against the Applicant should be concrete and precise.

If it is found that the allegations are made without providing any specific details or describing any particular instance of harassment, in such cases, where Informant did not mention date, time and place or manner in which the alleged harassment is rkn 7 apl 345.2020 new (1).odt occurred, the Court should be slow while holding that offence is made out against the applicants.

14. It is also held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the catena of cases that mere trivial irritations,
quarrels between spouses which happen in day-to-day married life not to be considered as cruelty.
The foundation of a sound marriage is tolerance, adjustment and respecting each other.

Therefore,
petty quibbles, trifling differences are general and should not be exaggerated and blown out of proportion to destroy the marriage.

15. In the light of the factual aspect of the matter and the settled position of law that, in such matrimonial cases, the Court should read the allegations in between the lines so as to do substantial justice and to take a pragmatic view of the matter.
16. In the light of settled principles of law, the perusal of allegation prima-facie demonstrate the fact that allegations are made with an oblique motive to implicate all the applicants in criminal offence.
It is specifically stated by Applicant No.1, he is mere 12 Standard passed, therefore there was no reason for him to demand the Family of Non-applicant No.2 to construct hospital for him.
The allegation of harassment during pregnancy period are not specific in nature.
All these allegation are vague and general in nature.

Matrimonial discord of non-applicant No.2 with the Applicants Family is well known to family members of non- applicant No.2 Family, but in their family meeting, it is not come on record that she was subjected to such cruelty that she cannot rkn 8 apl 345.2020 new (1).odt
cohabit with Husband, rather both the time, in view of compromise she went back to Applicant Family.
In respect of incidence dated 23/03/2018, it is clear that it was a case of food poisoning, but same was coloured as attempt to murder.

17. It will be relevant to refer the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Achin Gupta Vs State of Haryana and Another Reported in AIR 2024 S.C. 2548 , wherein it is observed in para- 31 as under:-
"31.

entities.text: Achin Gupta Vs State of Haryana and Another Reported in AIR 2024 S.C. 2548
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If the Court is convinced by the fact that the involvement by the complainant of her husband and his close relatives is with an oblique motive then even if the FIR and the chargesheet disclose the commission of a cognizable offence the Court with a view to doing substantial justice should read in between the lines the oblique motive of the complainant and take a pragmatic view of the matter.

If the submission canvassed by the counsel appearing for the Respondent No. 2 and the State is to be accepted mechanically then in our opinion the very conferment of the inherent power by the Cr.P.C. upon the High Court would be rendered otiose.

We are saying so for the simple reason that if the wife on account of matrimonial disputes decides to harass her husband and his family members then the first thing, she would ensure is to see that proper allegations are levelled in the First Information Report.

Many times the services of professionals are availed for the same and once the complaint is drafted by a legal mind, it would be very difficult thereafter to weed out any loopholes or rkn 9 apl 345.2020 new (1).odt other deficiencies in the same.

However, that does not mean that the Court should shut its eyes and raise its hands in helplessness, saying that whether true or false, there are allegations in the First Information Report and the chargesheet papers disclose the commission of a cognizable offence."
18. In the light of above, I am of the considered opinion that interference of this Court is necessary in the matter.
Keeping continue the criminal proceeding against applicants would nothing but abuse of process of law.
Hence, I proceed to pass the following order.
ORDER a] The criminal application is allowed.

b] The proceedings bearing Regular Criminal Case No. 182/2024 for the offence punishable under Sections 307, 498-A, 313, 504 and 506 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, arising out of Crime No. 0267/2019 registered with Police Station Washim (City), is hereby quashed and set aside.
19. Rue is made absolute in the aforesaid terms.
No order as to costs.
